evidence.baseline: It is a living process. And living processes are defined not by their freedom from error but by their capacity to perceive error and correct it. ... This is not a possibility we tolerate. It is a certainty we depend upon. The criticisms we have not yet heard are not threats to the project; they are the project's means of becoming what it is meant to be.
evidence.shipped: Providence should expect failure modes not named here. Real participants will discover where design cuts against purpose, where instruments misread, and where power hides.

findings.diagnosis: The deepest cut in the volume landed on the section that answers the whole chapter: why a catalogue of failures is not a counsel of despair. The shipped version keeps the prediction of unforeseen failure and drops the inversion that gives it force, error as the thing the project depends upon, along with the open-correction commitment, the commons argument, and the true-north close. What remains reads as a risk register's preamble. The full arc is restored: living process, expected wrongness, the one commitment, and what the correction is for.

findings.summary: The falsifiability limit is kept. This finding runs the other way.

evidence.baseline: Every genuine objection becomes a contribution. Every revealed flaw becomes the next thing repaired. The correction never ends, because the perceiving never ends, because the work is alive.
evidence.shipped: Every serious objection can contribute to better design, but not every objection can be absorbed without changing the thesis. Some evidence may require abandonment of a mechanism or claim. A living process is not one that survives every criticism. It is one capable of giving up what reality has disproved.

findings.authorizedBy: Not a defect. Recorded under R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT as a finding that runs the other way.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline's absorption doctrine has no stopping rule: every objection feeds the process and nothing can refute it, which quietly makes the living-process claim unfalsifiable, the exact posture the chapter's own measurement-failure section forswears. The kept paragraph supplies the stopping rule, abandonment of a mechanism or claim, in the section's own register, and its final sentence is the sharpest formulation of the volume's visible-limit discipline anywhere in the chapter. Kept in full as its own paragraph directly after the certainty-we-depend-upon paragraph, where it bounds the claim before the commitment builds on it. Seventh credited keep in the volume.

evidence.shipped: Correction requires more than openness to feedback. It requires channels through which criticism changes budgets, code, rules, leadership, and, when necessary, the decision to stop. People harmed by the system should not have to become unpaid researchers in order to be believed.

evidence.baseline: The living-process mark, the perceptions mark, the same-way mark, the many fence, and the meant-to-be mark.

findings.diagnosis: The living-process mark carried a turn into definition and became a period, the second movement opening on And. The perceptions mark introduced the three-part enumeration of new perceptions and became a colon. The same-way mark joined the dependent by-bringing phrase and became a comma. The many fence held the five-part appositive of who the many are and became paired commas. The meant-to-be mark introduced the closing triplet, one perception, one correction, one act of collective intelligence, and became a colon.
